description: The ideal-point heuristic estimates the remaining cost of a state as the vector `(h_1, …, h_N)`, where `h_i` is the exact shortest distance to a goal in objective `i` alone. Often no single path reaches this point, but no path can be better in any objective, so the estimate never overestimates. The crate builds it with one backward Dijkstra search per objective from the goal set. It is consistent and zero on goals, which the exact and approximate searches need; a state that reaches no goal gets no estimate and is pruned. It is the standard heuristic of multi-objective search; the reachable part of the graph must be finite.

papers.authors: Oren Salzman, Carlos Hernández Ulloa, Ariel Felner, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Multi-Objective Search: Algorithms, Applications, and Emerging Directions
